messages:
alisa: Morning handoff — quick summary of the thing we paged on overnight. TL;DR: embedding p95 jumped ~2.1s for a subset of traffic (about 5%), some downstream timeouts, cause was a routing policy change that sent a slice of traffic to a non-quantized variant after the 03:20 deploy. Full details and actions below.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: #INC-2026-1058 — p95 embedding latency > 1.5s for 5% of requests. Pager: sam, tori. Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-1058

sam: saw the initial alerts at ~03:25. Dashboard: embeddings p95 jumped to 2.8s, p50 steady. Error counts up a bit (502s from the model-worker).

devon: I rolled back the routing change at 03:36 (quick revert) but latency took a while to normalize due to cached KV state and warmed batchers.

mica: customers affected mostly on the eu-west region; passive reroute didn't catch them because the policy used a label mismatch. Investigating tagging rules now.

alisa: What I have so far in order: 1) deploy at 03:20 added new routing rule for "quantized-compat" flag 2) rule unintentionally matched requests missing the header, 3) those requests went to non-quantized variant with slower kernels resulting in higher tail latency.

sam: action items done overnight: patched policy to add explicit header check, kicked the embedding batcher on the affected pool, cleared prefix cache for the 03:20 cohort. Commands I ran: ```
# patch policy to require x-rw-quantized: true
rwctl routing update --id route-emb-quant --match 'headers.x-rw-quantized==true'
# restart batcher on pool eu-west-emb-2
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deploy/emb-batcher-eu-west-2
```

tori: I verified customer-facing errors decreased after the patch. Still seeing intermittent p95 at ~1.1s for a few minutes. I left the canary at 0.5% traffic to monitor.

devon: follow-ups needed: - add unit tests for header-matching when deploying routing rules - add synthetic checks to exercise quantized vs non-quantized paths every 10m - add a dashboard tile that breaks p95 by routing rule id

mica: noted a coverage gap: on-call runbook points to generic "routing" doc but no specific checklist for quantized routing. I'm adding a short runbook snippet under the embeddings playbook. Runbook link: https://console.redwood/runbooks/embeddings-latency (new section: routing-quantized-checklist).

alisa: Customer impact: two customers opened support tickets (IDs: 5682, 5690) — both are eu-west production workloads. We flagged both and sent proactive notes. No escalations to enterprise-support required yet.

deploy-bot: deploy 03:20 reported by pipeline: pipeline/infra-routing v1.12.4 -> success (triggered-by: devon). Full changelog: https://ci.redwood/pipelines/infra-routing/1.12.4

sam: Post-mortem timeline draft (short): 03:20 deploy adds routing rule; 03:25 Alerting fires; 03:30 initial triage; 03:36 revert routing change; 03:40 patch routing to header-check; 04:05 batcher restart and cache clear; 04:30 metrics mostly back to baseline; 08:00 final verification and tickets updated.

tori: On-call coverage notes: I'm primary until 12:00 UTC, devon is secondary until 12:00 UTC. Alisa will take swing at 16:00 UTC. If anything pages that looks similar, escalate to mica for routing rules follow-up.

alisa: Remaining open items for next shift: 1) add automated synthetic that pumps small embedding requests through quantized + non-quantized variants and compares tail latency (owner: devon) 2) add runbook checklist and link it in the incident template (owner: mica) 3) create alert that triggers when p95 diff between routing-rule buckets > 0.8s (owner: sam) 4) follow up with enterprise-support on the two customer notes (owner: tori).

devon: I'll put up a PR with the synthetic monitor by end of day and add tests for router-match logic. PR link: https://git.redwood/routing/pulls/402 (WIP).

mica: adding runbook snippet now, will ping in #eng-docs when done.

sam: logging note: we should include routing.rule_id in our long tail traces for embeddings, currently only model.variant shows. I'll open a ticket to add that field to trace headers.

alisa: Anything else before I handover? If not, I'll mark this thread as "handoff: resolved->monitoring" and leave the oncall playbook link: https://confluence.redwood/ops/oncall-playbook.

devon: all good from infra side, monitoring steady.

tori: ok — I'm good. Leaving primary coverage notes above.

mica: done with docs update, left a short checklist and a note linking this incident.

alisa: Thanks team. Passing to the next shift: primary=tori, secondary=devon until 00:00 UTC tomorrow. Monitor embeddings p95 and support inbox for any follow-ups. :thumbsup:
